open_points.subject: Project, Customer, Room and ArtifactPointer lifecycles
open_points.text: R0-89 says "every change after it is lost" when a pre-change backup replaces the store, while M01 says anonymisation is "final" and "`active` is never returned to", M03 says a room is "never changed, never removed", M04 says erasure is "written once and final", and M05 says superseding and withdrawal are "final".
open_points.question: Are these lifecycle and persistence guarantees scoped only to one store history, so restoring an older backup may resurrect earlier model states or remove models created later?
options: All lifecycle guarantees are per store history; restoration may roll back any model fact or existence
Some facts remain final across restoration and must be reconstructed outside the restored store
The finality statements remain absolute, contradicting R0-89
open_points.default_guess: Treat every lifecycle guarantee as scoped to the current store history and allow the restored backup to determine all model facts and existence.

open_points.subject: AgentSession access after restore
open_points.text: R0-46 says "Revoking a project blocks every later operation on it in that session", but R0-89 says a restored store loses "every change" made after the backup.
open_points.question: If a backup predates a revocation, project erasure, active-project change or grant, does the restored AgentSession access exactly revert to the backup, including restoring a grant and permitting later operations that the lost history had revoked?
options: Access facts revert exactly to the backup and checks use the restored granted set
Revocations and project-erasure removals must survive restoration through some separate fact
All session access is discarded when a restored store starts
open_points.default_guess: Restore the AgentSession facts exactly as recorded in the backup and authorize against that restored state.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry erasure lifecycle
open_points.text: R0-66 says that erasing audit entries means "every entry older than the date the owner gives is gone", and M09 gives `written -> erased`, while R0-89 says changes after the restored backup, "the audit entries with it", are lost.
open_points.question: May restoring a backup made before an audit erasure make the erased AuditEntry records readable again in the new store history?
options: Yes; audit erasure is final only within one store history
No; erased entries must remain erased across restored backups using state outside the store
Such a backup may not be restored
open_points.default_guess: Allow the entries present in the restored backup to reappear, treating erasure as final only within its original store history.

open_points.subject: Store history and AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: R0-89 says "That store begins its own history from the backup" and that log numbering holds "within each store's history"; M09 says the sequence number is minted by Registry and "is what tells them apart", but no store-history identity or fact is defined.
open_points.question: Is a store history merely an implicit scope, making an AuditEntry identity the sequence number within the currently installed history, or must Registry mint and retain a history identity so entries from pre-loss and post-restore histories remain distinguishable?
options: History is implicit; AuditEntry identity is scoped to the current store history
Add a durable store-history identity and make AuditEntry identity include or reference it
Treat the restored store as continuing the old history despite the branching sequence numbers
open_points.default_guess: Use the store history as an implicit identity scope and add no StoreHistory model or persisted history identifier.
